h: Castles, Lochs and a Pirate's Afternoon
p: A pirate-themed course practically begs for a bit of extra storytelling, so why not turn the round into a proper adventure? Give everyone a pirate name before you tee off, appoint a captain to keep the scorecard, and decide that the loser has to walk the plank (well, buy the ice creams). It costs nothing and turns a round of mini golf into a game the kids will be talking about all the way home.

Adventure golf rewards patience over power. Most holes are designed with a clever route around the obstacles, so look at the slope and the walls before you swing, and don't be afraid of using a bank shot. A gentle tap that rolls to the edge of the hole is usually better than a big whack that bounces straight out the other side. Younger players can stand closer or take an extra shot without anyone minding.

If your crew is fired up by galleons and treasure, the real-life history around Motherwell is a short drive away. Bothwell Castle, near Uddingston, is a vast red sandstone ruin high above the River Clyde, with a mighty round keep and centuries of sieges behind it. It's run by Historic Environment Scotland and makes a cracking outing for kids who've just spent an afternoon pretending to be buccaneers.

Closer to the course, Strathclyde Country Park is ideal for a breather. Strathclyde Loch has long, flat paths for strolling and scooting, and you might spot rowers or sailors gliding along the water, which feels very fitting after a round on Devil's Island.
